svg.title: AegisWeb architecture: page understanding is separate from browser-action authority
svg.desc: A task router sends a request to a page-understanding pipeline, a browser-action pipeline, or both. Understanding retrieves evidence and may only highlight validated content blocks. Actions are proposed by a local model, strictly validated, re-checked against a fresh page snapshot, authorized by a deterministic capability gate and then executed. A trust boundary keeps content block IDs from becoming action targets. Mail-composer pages use a separate adapter that does not pass through the authorization gate.
svg.text: Page understanding and browser actions are separate pipelines · only the action pipeline touches the page, and only through the gate
no authority: can read, retrieve and highlight; cannot act
authority: every proposal is validated, re-checked and authorized before it runs
content block IDs never become action targets
MIXED only: the preflight (sidepanel/agent-preflight.ts) either lets
the browser stage start, or blocks it with INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
re-observe after every action · stops after 8 model steps (PARTIAL)
useAgentActions.ts calls controller.composeEmail directly; it does not pass through authorizeAction.
authorizeAction is called only from slm/execution.ts (re-checked every time this diagram is built).
WHERE IT RUNS · CHROME MV3 EXTENSION
builds both snapshots, performs the approved
Team project: Codefest Chitwan 2026 repository, four or more contributors. Drawn from the source tree and checked against it; paths are relative to src/.
Sudeep's commits (14 to 16 Aug): local model adapter and Qwen3-4B WebLLM setup, DOM snapshot extraction and model-context adapter, Playwright browser controller, shared
action and security contracts, runtime-stage reporting.
Most capability-gate commits are a teammate's. Planned latency, security-gate and adversarial benchmarks are not completed; no benchmark is claimed here.
